report_title: Infomaniak Bug Bounty - Validated Findings Report
method: Read-only HTTP header analysis, content type verification

vulnerabilities.title: CORS Misconfiguration - Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *

evidence.observations: Multiple applications returning CORS wildcard without explicit methods/credentials configuration

proof_of_concept: Impact: CORS wildcard allows any origin to read cross-origin responses. If an authenticated user visits a malicious site, the site can read data from API responses if cookies are sent.
Note: Requires data endpoint with sensitive information to be exploitable. Current finding is configuration-level issue.
Verification: Request with Origin: evil.com returns header - Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
remediation: 1. Replace Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with specific origin(s) (e.g. https://www.infomaniak.com)
2. Implement dynamic allow-list if multiple origins are required
3. Add explicit Access-Control-Allow-Methods header (e.g. GET, POST, OPTIONS)
4. Add explicit Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true or false (prefer false)
5. Add proper CORS preflight handling with OPTIONS method
6. Review if any endpoints should not be accessible cross-origin at all

vulnerabilities.title: API Endpoint Misconfiguration - Returning HTML Instead of JSON
proof_of_concept: Impact: Applications expecting JSON will fail to parse, or HTML content may be interpreted as data.
Security risk: If endpoints handle sensitive data, the misfiled content could expose internal structure.
Note: These are infrastructure/API endpoints that should serve structured data, not HTML.
remediation: 1. Change Content-Type header to application/json for all API endpoints
2. Ensure API routes return proper JSON responses, not HTML templates
3. Implement consistent error handling that returns JSON error responses
4. Verify API route handlers return correct Content-Type
5. Add Content-Security-Policy header for additional security
6. Review and remove HTML template fallback for JSON API routes
